target: Primer Product Dialog transient content, task use and contextual presentation/size variants
observed_behavior: Primer's product Dialog page describes a floating surface for transient content such as confirmation actions and selection choices. Its documented examples include default, optional subtitle, footer buttons, right-side sheet, and responsive narrow-viewport bottom-sheet positioning. The guidance gives small for very little content, medium for typical tasks like forms/selection, and larger variants for more horizontal space; before an extra-large dialog it asks whether a full page would be more suitable. It says the body scrolls if the maximum dialog height is reached.
context: W07 Stage B5 K3; authorized Primer product page section: Dialog overview; React examples — side sheet, responsive bottom sheet, size variants. Explanatory product API/design documentation within Primer only.
limitations: These are product-specific Primer surface/size conventions, not a rule that every transient interaction requires a Dialog.
Extra-large Dialog is explicitly qualified by the alternative of navigating to a dedicated page; this context must not be omitted.
Examples use Primer React component API and are not live viewport, animation, responsive, keyboard or accessibility measurements.
Neither product docs nor visible 'ready' labels establish parity with the pinned W07-S6 React implementation or with a particular deployed application.
